nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template environment file defining Neo4j connection variables (URI, username, password, database) for both local bolt and Neo4j Aura cloud deployments; used by docker-compose and the graph exporter.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: JARVIS operations manual governing all work under jarvis/ — defines the read-only consumer contract, the dev_graph projection chain (Neo4j + two graph.json copies), component class boundary rules, backend safety invariants, and re-projection workflow.

nodes.name: JARVIS_INTEGRATION_ROADMAP.md
nodes.summary: Five-stage integration and refactor roadmap (ADR-010) for JARVIS covering the graph.json exporter bridge, graph-driven console, React/Vite/TypeScript refactor, LLM GraphRAG /ask endpoint, and voice bridge with single-URL serving.

nodes.name: PROJECTION_SYNC_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Technical plan addressing drift between dev_graph markdown projections (Neo4j, frontend/graph.json, hud/public/graph.json) with four concrete recommendations: eliminate duplicate graph.json, consolidate resync into one script, optional pre-commit hook, and dashboard chrome contract.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Developer guide for the JARVIS dev_graph stack covering prerequisites, offline quick start, full docker-compose containerized setup, wiring into the JARVIS console, React HUD run instructions, and notes on migrating to Neo4j Aura.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Docker Compose stack defining three services — Neo4j 5 Community (with APOC, remapped to ports 7475/7688), a read-only FastAPI graph API on port 8000, and an nginx-served static frontend on port 8080 — with external named volumes for a pre-populated graph store.
nodes.languageNotes: Host ports are remapped off defaults (7474/7687) to avoid collisions with another Neo4j container on the host; in-compose service communication uses internal ports unchanged.

nodes.name: resync-devgraph.ps1
nodes.summary: Fail-fast PowerShell script that atomically re-projects the dev_graph markdown into all downstream consumers: validates with sync_to_neo4j.py --dry-run, re-projects Neo4j with --clear, then re-writes both graph.json copies via export_graph_json.py; supports -NoNeo4j flag for offline use.

nodes.name: start.ps1
nodes.summary: Idempotent PowerShell launcher that starts the JARVIS HUD at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ by ensuring Neo4j is running, building the React HUD once if dist/ is missing, then starting the FastAPI bridge via uvicorn in the foreground.
